label: digit 0 input at late original positions (t >= 5)
explanation: Fires when the input token is the digit 0 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 5 or later (orig_idx 5-8). It never fires on 0 at positions 0-4, on any other token, on the delimiter step, or in the copy phase (apart from a few tiny ~0.02 activations). Every 0 at t>=5 activates it (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude grows with position: mean activation per active step rises about 4x from t=5 to t=8, and the top examples are all 0 at t=8 in L=9 sequences. Low-quartile examples are 0 at t=5 in short (L=5-6) sequences.

issues: Test score for the predicate: precision 1.0, recall 0.9997, F1 0.9998, mass recall 0.99999. The 9 missed activations on test are tiny (0.02-0.03 of max) and scattered across the last original step and the delimiter, with no pattern. There are no false positives.

The other claims hold. Every active step outside a 0 input is negligible: 1 in the copy phase, 0 on the delimiter, 0 on any 0 at t<5. All active steps fall at orig_idx 5-8, where the firing rate is a flat 0.033, which is exactly a 0 at that position. Mean activation per active step rises about 3.8x from t=5 to t=8 (0.186/10963 vs 0.177/2763). The top examples are all a 0 at t=8 in L=9 sequences.

Minor wording error: the low-quartile examples are a 0 at t=5, but they are not only in L=5-6 sequences. One is L=7 ('d e p h q 0 o'). Also, no sequence of length 5 can contain t=5, so 'L=5-6' really means L=6. This does not affect the verdict.
